result:
I looked at all four renders and read the correction plan, technical closure, export audit and predecessor review. **I'd hold winter v2 back from human review as it stands: one visible defect needs fixing or explaining first.** I changed nothing, approved nothing and transferred no animation.

## The defect: a green rectangle on the lower front hull
- **What it is:** in the `front` view of `pbr-r1.png`, the plate between the tracks below the upper glacis is dark olive green with hard, straight edges. It's still obvious in `recognition-256-r1.png`.
- **Why it isn't just shadow:** a shadow on white paint would look neutral or blue-grey like the rest of the shading. This is clearly green, so it looks like a paint area the white coat never reached.
- **Why the evidence missed it:**
  - The front view is the only one that shows the plate. The front three-quarter camera sits too high to see it.
  - The plan's first acceptance check only covers "turret sides or rear hull", so the front plate was never in scope.
  - The predecessor review called this plate "nearly black in every finish… inherited". At this render size it reads green on a white tank, and the brief is a clean, even whitewash.
  - Hash checks that confirm the parts and paint areas are unchanged would preserve a missed area like this, not catch it.
- **What I couldn't confirm:** which material or paint role causes it, or whether it's a deliberate tonal step. Even if it is deliberate, it reads as a raw green patch, the same kind of fault as the old objection.
- **Proposed fix:** a paint-only change, either adding the lower front plate to the whitewash or giving it a neutral shade of the same white. Then re-render the front view.

## Did the even coat close the old green patch-edge objection?
- **Turret side and rear hull: yes, visually.** The predecessor's objection was a hard vertical edge on the turret side and a straight-edged rear-hull patch. In the physical-left and rear three-quarter views both areas are now even white with no colour breaks. I'm basing this on the images, not on the closure file's argument that "constant colours mean no projection seam".
- **The whole vehicle: no.** The same kind of fault, a hard-edged green area, still shows on the front.

## Other checks
- **Hatches and deck:** both cupola rings, the hatch-lid seam lines and the driver hatch still read. Next to the approved desert top view, though, the deck panel lines and turret-roof panel breaks have mostly gone in the white. The plan's "restrained part-role tonal separation" is barely visible. That's acceptable but weak. It's not blocking.
- **White against the background:** contrast against the pale blue-grey backdrop is low, and the top-view outline edges blur slightly. The dark tracks, wheels and grilles plus the cast shadow keep the outline readable at 256 px.
- **M2 and M240:** both keep their dark receivers, barrels and cradles, matching the desert source. Their character is intact.
- **Seams and missing materials:** I saw no magenta or untextured surfaces and no seams anywhere else. The physical-right side looks greyer than the left, which matches the lighting in earlier sheets, so it isn't a defect.
- **The 128 px evidence is weak:** `recognition-128-r1.png` is the whole contact sheet shrunk down, with the header text cut off. Each tank is only about 40 px wide, so it shows overall shape but doesn't really test recognition at 128 px per view.
- **What I couldn't verify:** with Read only, I couldn't hash the PNGs against `technical-closure-r1.json`.

## Strongest case for scoring each category below 3/4
| Category | Strongest case for below 3 | Resolved? |
|---|---|---|
| Identity recognition | An all-white coat removes paint cues, and the 128 px proof is a shrunk-down sheet. | **Yes, scores 3.** The geometry (wedge turret, bustle rack, skirts, bore evacuator, two roof guns) is identical to the approved desert source and reads at 256 px. |
| Silhouette | White against the pale background gives the lowest edge contrast so far. | **Borderline 3.** Dark running gear and shadows carry the outline, but this backdrop isn't the in-game one. Worth testing on a snow-like background. |
| Mechanical coherence | White on white flattens deck panels and hatch outlines, and the green plate looks like a part that doesn't belong. | **Partly.** Hatches, cupolas and weapons read; deck panels are weakened. It scores 3 only once the green plate is fixed. |
| Production integrity | A hard-edged green area left outside the whitewash on the main front view. | **Not resolved. Scores 2 until it's corrected or explained.** Geometry, parents, steel/rubber/glass and zero textures all check out, but technical checks can't clear a visible fault. |

## Bottom line
- **Blocking defect:** the green lower front plate is clearly visible and goes against both the "clean even whitewash" brief and the plan's own "no green-island" choice. I can see the defect; I haven't confirmed its cause.
- **Human review:** not yet. Fix the plate in a paint-only revision and re-render the front view, then send it to human review. If you want the human reviewer to see it now anyway, present it with this defect stated as a known blocker.
